observations: A luminous orange jellyfish-shaped body with long trailing filaments floats in the blue sky above a dark coastal inlet.
The rocky shoreline, small buildings and water below form an otherwise recognisable nighttime landscape.
effect: Moving a marine form into the sky may make an ordinary coastal view feel strange and invite a second look.
teaching_value: Contemporary photomontage makes a clear change of setting while leaving the environment recognisable.
ambiguity: The luminous body can also resemble a comet; the reading does not establish a message or creator intent.

observations: A human portrait is divided by a square grid, with some tiles showing sky or dark equipment instead of uninterrupted skin and clothing.
Fine polygon meshes and a network of connected circles overlap the face, neck, coat and background.
effect: Treating a person as tiles, meshes and connections may suggest that human identity is being translated into measurable data.
teaching_value: A contemporary editorial composite fuses portraiture with the visual vocabulary of quantification.
ambiguity: The visual reading is a proposal; source metadata separately describes the image as a metaphor for AI quantification.

observations: A tall stack of black top hats rests on a red fire hydrant beside a parked car.
A standing man reaches up toward the stack in an ordinary street setting.
effect: Using a fire hydrant as a stand for an excessive tower of hats may interrupt expectations of an ordinary street scene.
teaching_value: Observational street photography shows contextual mismatch without requiring a digital composite.
ambiguity: The photograph does not establish whether this was storage, performance or promotion; visible branding is not an endorsement.

observations: A dark eagle spreads its wings across a pale printed field.
The pale spaces beside the wings have forehead, nose and chin-like profiles sharing the eagle's contours.
Small printed words below ask the viewer what they see in the picture.
effect: Switching attention from the dark bird to the pale face profiles may make the same contours support alternating subjects.
teaching_value: A historical printed card shows how the gap beside a positive silhouette can become a second recognisable figure.
ambiguity: Recognising the historical identities requires source context; the observed mechanism is the shared eagle/profile contour.

observations: A woman sits at a dressing table facing her reflection in a large rounded mirror.
The two dark hair masses resemble eye sockets; the mirror outline and pale tabletop combine into a large skull-like face.
effect: Combining a grooming scene with a skull-like form may connect appearance and self-regard with mortality.
teaching_value: A graphic double image links two concepts through an overall shape assembled from ordinary scene details.
ambiguity: This is a compound image, not a clean positive/negative contour reversal, so it is not counted toward figure-ground ambiguity.

observations: A large caterpillar sits upright on a mushroom and holds a smoking pipe connected to a hookah.
A small girl stands beside the mushroom looking toward the caterpillar.
effect: Giving an insect a seated human activity and an elaborate smoking device may make the garden setting feel fantastical.
teaching_value: Narrative illustration creates mismatch by assigning a familiar human activity to an animal.
ambiguity: Within the fictional world this can be normal; incongruity depends on comparison with everyday expectations.

observations: A historical chart depicts a temple interior whose columns, ceiling and floor recede toward a distant point.
Names, dates and labelled categories occupy the architectural surfaces and repeated columns.
effect: Mapping historical time onto a walk through architectural space may turn an abstract chronology into a place the viewer can mentally explore.
teaching_value: An information graphic uses architecture as a spatial metaphor, broadening the collection beyond pictorial allegory.
ambiguity: The chart's historical selection is culturally partial; small text is not fully readable in the reduced starter copy.

observations: An enormous stemmed goblet stands in a rocky mountain landscape.
Its bowl contains water, tiny sailing boats and a tree-lined rim; water spills from the rim into the terrain below.
effect: Making a drinking vessel large enough to contain a landscape may disrupt familiar scale and turn the object into an imagined world.
teaching_value: A painted object/environment mismatch offers a distinct mechanism from animal personification, street anomalies and sky photomontage.
ambiguity: Possible allegorical meanings are not established by these visible details.
